item.title: Several Minor Things
item.description:
Well, I have been busy trying to get this site a bit more user friendly.

Headings

The headings now have a distinctive font that I thought they really needed to help them stand out a bit more. I also really like the all caps sharpie on masking tape look of the font. I know it’s not for everyone, but I get to pick so here we are.

Sidebar

The sidebar now shows a lot of information like the original date of pages, last modified dates, lists of tags and links. Since I do not have any search functionality, and don’t plan to try adding one, I think it’s important to at least provide taxonomy links to help people find things.

item.title: Ghost in the Shell (1995)
item.description: Written before the mass adoption of the internet, before the social and technological terms we all are now comfortable with (and in many cases were born into). This is a story about a law enforcement team on the cutting edge of what the 80s thought today’s tech was going to be like. Cybernetic implants, smart tracker bullets, remote mind wipes, optical camouflage, the works. The story chronicles inter-agency turf wars played at the highest level, and the emergency of a new kind of criminal. It does this while asking deep questions about what it means to be a human, a distinct person, in a connection and increasingly synthetic world.

item.title: Using SearXNG as You Default Search
item.description:
SearXNG is a meta search engine that you run locally. It provides very fast results without a lot of fluff and tracking. You can fine-tune it to only use certain sources, search certain material types, skip social media, or even exclusively search social media. It is a fantastic tool and something anyone with the inclination and resources should consider setting up.

Setting up the Service

My setup is a lot more complicated than it absolutely has to be. But, you wouldn’t be here if you wanted the generic guide.

item.title: The Cuckoos Egg
item.description: The Cuckoo’s Egg is the autobiographical account of an astronomy student who’s grant ran out so he got a job in the university’s IT department. A 75 cent discrepancy in the accounting software would lead him down a rabbit hole of hackers, military and national security systems, and academia. This all being told from the author’s experiences it is a fascinating tale of the very real world of cyber security in the twilight years of the Cold War.

item.title: Project: Majel
item.description:
Majel Barrett (Rodenberry) was a pillar of Star Trek, having been in the original pilot, given a new role for the series, and then going on to make appearances in both The Next Generation and Deep Space 9 while also voicing the standard Starfleet computer. It is as tribute to her I name this Project: Majel.

What is Project: Majel?

Everyone who grew up watching Star Trek will remember the voice interactions with the computer, and how the computer was able to flawlessly understand what was being said and know what needed to be done, and then carry out the actions required. That is a high bar to aim for, but climbing towards it I hope to still learn a great deal, and to provide actual value to my household and the growing community of Local LLM enthusiasts.

item.title: Minimum Viable Product
item.description: Well, this is my first post and as the title suggests it is really just something to have something. I am working on stuff like taxonomies, front matter, and the like. I don’t really want the main focus of this site to be blog posts, and really certain I have very much to say in a diary format that I 1. think other people will want to read, and 2. want to share publicly. Maybe that will change and I’ll start considering myself an influencer… yeah, probably not.

item.title: Ghost in the Shell (2026)
item.description:
Oh man, I had really high hopes from the trailer. I had high hopes.

The opening text went by at blink and you miss it speed. Luckily, it was faithfully pulled from the original manga, which was sitting on the bookshelf next to me. And that was the tone throughout. On one had you get a highly faithful rendering of the source material, while simultaneously it is being warped in odd ways that I did not care for. Muted color space and textures on a gritty realistic background, but saturated and vibrant color on characters who art style would seamlessly ramp from 1990s anime to (what I think of as) Rick and Morty and back again. It was jarring and made it impossible to fully sit in the material and enjoy the show.
